clue.text: Taste a little lamb in something curried

indicators.note: the small piece of lamb is put inside the thing that gets curried, so 'in' places one within the other

parts.note: people curry favour, so favour is the thing that is curried

indicators.note: just a little of the word lamb is wanted here, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cook adds a small amount of lamb to a curry for extra savour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something curried' looks like a dish, but it points to the idiom 'curry favour'. 'In' puts L, from 'a little lamb', inside FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste or savour of food is its characteristic flavour; the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Well-known fellow, largely an animal

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a mouse is an animal

explanation.surface: A man known to everyone is described as mostly beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' means most of the word, so the animal loses its last letter; 'fellow' looks like the subject but is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being famous means being widely known, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He's first on way out, at least

indicators.note: out suggests being disordered, so the letters are rearranged
first means the opening letter of He's

explanation.surface: A man insists he will be first on the road out, at minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H, the first of He's, with ON and WAY, and 'out' rearranges all six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are used to qualify a statement in the sense of 'in any case' or 'at any rate'.

clue.text: Bottom's part, taking full expression too far

definitions.text: Bottom's part, taking full expression too far

parts.words: Bottom's part, taking full expression too far
parts.note: the middle of the word bottom holds a familiar three-letter abbreviation; spelt out in full it is a phrase meaning too far

explanation.surface: The weaver Bottom overacts his role, giving every line full rein.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT sits inside bOTTom; 'taking full expression' says expand the abbreviation, and 'too far' defines it. The surface recalls Bottom the ham actor in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over the top means going too far or overdoing things.

clue.text: Large animals do OK with what may get up one's nose

definitions.text: what may get up one's nose

parts.note: rhinoceroses, shortened in the usual way, are large animals
to cope is to manage or get by, to do OK

explanation.surface: Big beasts manage fine with something that irritates the nostrils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up one's nose' is a British idiom for annoy, but here it is literal: the instrument is inserted into the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medical instrument for examining the nasal passages, so it literally goes up the nose.

clue.text: Very large maternal pair leaving emergency room

parts.note: mam is a homely word for one's mother

indicators.note: the hospital department's letters walk out of the pair of words, so leaving signals removal

parts.note: the second maternal word is mother itself

explanation.surface: Mother and grandmother walk out of a hospital casualty ward together.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'maternal pair' is two words for mother, MAM and MOTHER; 'leaving' takes the ER out of the end of MOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mammoth was an enormous prehistoric elephant, so as an adjective the word means huge or gigantic.

clue.text: Electronic component beginning to make one large animal cool

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of make

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a croc, short for crocodile, is a large animal
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Making a big beast seem trendy starts with a little electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One large animal' reads as a single beast, but 'one' is the Roman numeral and the animal is a crocodile in short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny integrated circuit is a basic electronic component.

clue.text: Animal without wings, swimming in the sea

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement and disorder, so the letters are rearranged
wings are the outer letters of the word, so they are cut away

explanation.surface: A creature with no wings is swimming in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without wings' trims Animal to NIMA, and 'swimming' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the main' is an old poetic term for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Covered once again, face up

parts.note: over can mean again, as in do it over

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read the letters upwards, reversing them

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: A face has been covered all over again and turned upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns DIAL into LAID in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlaid means covered with a layer of something, as with gold leaf.

clue.text: 10 in head's strangely gone more quickly

indicators.note: the number goes inside the rearranged letters
strangely tells us the letters of head's are rearranged

parts.note: the number is written out as the word ten

explanation.surface: A ten in someone's head makes them disappear oddly faster.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it is just the number TEN, inserted into HASED, the rearranged HEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: If you have hastened you have gone faster, sped up.

clue.text: Pair of smalls flying from foreign embassy, perhaps

indicators.note: the two small-size letters fly away out of the word embassy, so they are removed
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small, and a pair gives two of them

explanation.surface: Two pairs of underwear are flying out of an overseas embassy, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear, which steers the surface; here it is two S abbreviations. Take SS from EMBASSY to leave EMBAY, and 'foreign' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and maybe are interchangeable adverbs expressing possibility.

clue.text: Catty talk? B___ off, it's irritating

definitions.note: the clue's adjective stands for the noun meaning the quality of being irritating, the condition of an irritated skin

indicators.note: B___ off reads as an instruction to take the B away from the front of the catty word

parts.note: bitchiness is spiteful, catty talk
the letter B with the rest of a rude word blanked out

explanation.surface: Someone tells a spiteful gossip to clear off because their nastiness is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B___ off' looks like a censored curse, but it is the instruction: drop the B from BITCHINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchiness is a skin irritation; the clue uses 'it's irritating' loosely to describe that sensation.

clue.text: Eccentric moving to Honduras after losing a second farm animal

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift around, so they are rearranged
the letters of a and second's abbreviation are taken away from the travel phrase before rearranging

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal used for draught work

explanation.surface: An odd character relocates to Central America once a second farm animal has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges the letters of 'to Honduras' once 'after losing' has taken out a and second's abbreviation, giving UNORTHOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eccentric departs from accepted behaviour, which is what unorthodox describes.

clue.text: Large animals start to hibernate in right-wing country

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK's right-wing Conservative Party

indicators.note: the opening letter of hibernate goes inside the name of the country

parts.note: Wales is one of the countries of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: start to points at the first letter of hibernate

explanation.surface: Big creatures settle down for winter sleep in a conservative nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics blue is the Conservative Party's colour, which is why it stands for right-wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The species named is the largest animal that has ever lived, so 'large animals' is a fair plural description.

clue.text: Off/on, hard/soft etc

indicators.note: off suggests being out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of switches and textures runs off/on, hard/soft and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like part of the list of opposites; it rearranges ON HARD SOFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc. is short for et cetera, meaning and the rest, and so on.

clue.text: Very large animal initially kept in pen (hint: eel's wrong)

indicators.note: the animal's first letter is kept inside the scrambled letters, as if in a pen
wrong tells us the letters of pen, hint and eel are put in the wrong order
initially means take the first letter of animal

explanation.surface: A big beast is penned up, and a note says the eel is in the wrong enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after eel is just 'is', so 'eel's wrong' means the eel is wrong. 'Pen' tempts as the definition of an enclosure, but it is only letters to rearrange, with A tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephantine means like an elephant in size, hence enormous or huge.

clue.text: Female animal in poem not having its tail disappear

parts.note: Eva is a female name

indicators.note: the animal goes inside the shortened poem
the poem loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, the word poem itself
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A female creature vanishes from a poem that lacks its ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female animal' wants to be one creature such as a doe; it is two pieces, a woman's name and a rodent. 'Not having its tail' leaves POE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to vanish like vapour, hence to disappear.

clue.text: Scary, meatless breed of cattle

indicators.note: meatless says a word for a meat is taken away from the breed

parts.note: Chillingham cattle are a rare wild breed from Northumberland in England

explanation.surface: A rare type of cow, with no meat on it, is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: Chillingham cattle are an ancient wild herd in northern England; take away HAM, a meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chilling is frightening enough to send a shiver down the spine.

clue.text: Mounted odd piece in Tate Modern

parts.note: mounted can mean up, as when on horseback

indicators.note: the piece goes inside the gallery's name
piece means only part of the word odd is used, with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A strange artwork has been hung in a famous London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tate Modern' is a London gallery, but 'Modern' is the definition; 'piece' trims odd to OD and 'in' places it inside Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date means current or modern.

clue.text: Part of brain for studying large animals?

parts.note: a hippo is a large African animal; the clue's plural just reads as a place for them
a campus is the grounds of a university, a place for studying

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the head is a university for large animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a CAMPUS for HIPPOs. The question mark admits the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the seahorse-shaped region of the brain that deals with memory, a genuine anatomical part.

clue.text: Large animal devours Lawrence, member of shooting party

indicators.note: devours means the animal swallows the other letters

parts.note: a bear is a large animal
TE are the initials of T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A large beast eats a man called Lawrence during a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: A beater drives game birds towards the guns on a British shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: On a shoot, beaters flush out the game, so a beater belongs to the shooting party.

clue.text: See 12
Large animal found in very large numbers

indicators.note: the animal is found inside the word for a very large number, once its first three letters are dropped

parts.note: a thousand thousand, and its bigger cousins, all end in the same four letters

explanation.surface: A big beast is said to roam in huge numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal sits at the end of MILLION, BILLION and TRILLION; dropping MIL from MILLION shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat of Africa is a classic example of a large animal.

clue.text: Point in golf shoes sporting pimple effect?

indicators.note: the compass point goes inside the rearranged footwear letters
sporting suggests playful activity, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A golfer's spiked shoes leave a pattern of little bumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' rearranges GOLF SHOES and 'in' slips E, a compass point, among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose-pimples are the bumpy skin effect from cold or fear, so 'pimple effect' describes it with a question mark.

clue.text: See 4
Girl in the middle of wearing very large animal's head

indicators.note: the middle letter of wearing is wanted

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

indicators.note: head means the first letter of animal

explanation.surface: A girl is wearing the head of a huge creature.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the middle of weaRing, then OS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain example: Rosa is a common female forename, so it fits the generic definition 'girl'.

clue.text: Over in Ascot, a Romanian lover

indicators.note: over means the letters are read backwards, turned over
the letters sit inside the run Ascot, a Romanian

explanation.surface: Over at the Ascot races, a Romanian romancer turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'ascOT A ROMANIan'; 'Over' signals the turn and 'in' says the letters lie within.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover or sweetheart, borrowed from Italian.

clue.text: Speed reached by large animal

indicators.note: the speed word is reached by the large letter coming after it

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A large beast hits a certain velocity.
explanation.walkthrough: The ratel is the honey badger of Africa and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce carnivorous mammal, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Bomb found in garden near deer, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly says take the odd-numbered letters across the three words

explanation.surface: Something explosive turns up in the garden beside a deer, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: Take letters 1, 3, 5 and so on through 'garden near deer': G R E N A D E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown bomb.

clue.text: Former model consumed by unfulfilled animal urges

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the model letter is swallowed inside the cut-down animal
unfulfilled means the animal is not complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a horse is an animal
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: A former model's appetite is swallowed by an animal's frustrated cravings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Henry Ford's famous early car, so 'model' gives T; 'unfulfilled' leaves HORS for it to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort someone is to urge them strongly; both verbs mean to press or encourage.
